footnotes.text: 2. Some colleges require a minimum GPA for major courses. Courses indicated in this column are included in the major GPA for this program of study.

footnotes.text: 3. Students in the Comparative Literature major are required to demonstrate proficiency in two foreign languages. Students must reach proficiency equivalent to the 300-level literature course prerequisites in the first foreign language, and equivalent to the 122 course in the second language, through course credit. Students who begin at the 109/110/121 level in the first foreign language may be required to complete courses in addition to those in this map in order to reach the 300-level language proficiency needed in preparation for the Literature courses in the first foreign language. Students who test out of the 122-level of a second foreign language will be required to take a higher-level course in the language.

Whichever is not fulfilled through the Carolina Core GHS requirement must be fulfilled through this college requirement.

footnotes.text: 6. The cognate is intended to support the course work in the major. The cognate must consist of twelve hours of courses at the advanced level, outside of, but related to the major. A second major eliminates the minor/cognate requirement.

footnotes.text: 7. Examples of foreign language literature courses include, but are not limited to: FREN 450, 451, 452, and 453 (if taught in French); GERM 420, 430, 440, 450, and 460 (if taught in German); ITAL 404 and 405 (if taught in Italian); PORT 312, 325, and 375 (if taught in Portuguese); RUSS 319L and 320L (if taught in Russian); SPAN 375, 404, and 405 (if taught in Spanish). Foreign language literature courses must be approved by an advisor.
